subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has the same view and next steps. Please feel free to correct or add anything.

Summary of pain points / goals we heard:
- Production p95 latency currently ~1.5s for single-turn responses; goal is <= 350ms p95 for the core interactive flow (chat + streaming)
- Streaming UX is important: tokens should appear as they generate, with max additional tail latency of ~100ms after model emits tokens
- Concurrency: peak concurrent users expected ~600 during realistic peak windows; baseline concurrent inference sessions ~150
- Throughput pattern: large portion of traffic is short prompt -> short response (avg tokens/sec low), but bursty spikes during market opens (10-15 minute bursts)
- Current stack: in-house endpoint running open LLM on GPU fleet with custom batching; logging/metrics are limited and there's frequent tokenization-induced latency variance

Success criteria you outlined:
- Demonstrable p95 <= 350ms on a 99th-percentile production workload (or clear plan to achieve it with Redwood Dedicated)
- Streaming token-by-token arrival with no noticeable reordering or long tail (>100ms)
- Sustained throughput to support 600 concurrent sessions with graceful degradation / fallback
- Visibility: per-route token-level cost and latency breakdowns for billing and CS monitoring

Next steps (agreed):
1) Alex to share sample load profile and a small set of representative prompts/trace files (you mentioned anonymized traces) — helpful to run a qualification test.
2) We (Redwood) to provide a qualification plan and proposed test matrix (p95, streaming tail, concurrency).
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/eng team (Aditya will lead) to review architecture and any security/compliance requirements.
4) If qualification looks good, follow-up with high-level pricing/commit proposal for Dedicated or hybrid routing.

Tentative schedule: qualification test week the week of Jun 21, deep-dive next Tue/Thu (please share availability).

Attachments: placeholder for any sample files you share — please send anonymized traces.

Thanks again — I’ll coordinate times once you share availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. Couple of clarifications and I attached a small sample load profile and anonymized traces.

Clarifications:
- Our current baseline p95 is measured at the API layer; we see ~1.5s under normal load, but under bursts (market open) p95 spikes to 2.8-3.2s.
- Streaming is currently client-side polling; we would benefit from server-initiated streaming or chunked responses to improve UX.
- Concurrency: 600 concurrent *active* sessions is peak, but sustained concurrently open sockets are closer to 150-200.

Attachments included: finly_load_profile.csv (sample QPS over 48h) and traces.zip (anonymized tokens and timestamps). I also attached a PNG of our simplified system architecture (finly_system_arch.png).

We are available for the deep-dive on Tue 2027-06-08 between 10:00-12:00 PDT. Looking forward to the qualification plan.

Alex

Perfect — got the files, thanks. Quick follow-up and a proposed test matrix below.

Proposed qualification test matrix (high level):
- Baseline p95 test: run your trace against a Redwood-hosted instance with the same model to measure end-to-end p95. Goal: show p95 <= 350ms or identify root causes (batching, tokenization, network).
- Streaming tail test: replay streaming-enabled sessions and measure token inter-arrival times and tail latency. Goal: median token latency <50ms, 95th <100ms.
- Concurrency stress test: ramp to 600 concurrent active sessions in 3 phases (150, 350, 600) and observe degradation; evaluate graceful fallback to smaller model / queuing policy.
- Cost and unit economics: per-token cost estimate for the observed workload under two configs: Dedicated reserved pool and Hybrid hosted+Dedic.

Immediate asks from Finly:
- A 24-48h sample trace (you provided) and a short list of 10 representative prompts we should prioritize.
- Team availability for the deep-dive on Tue 2027-06-08 10:00 PDT — we’ll put Aditya and our infra lead on the invite.

Aditya — I copied you for the technical kickoff. Can you please: (1) review the attached traces and load_profile, (2) propose an infra test harness (k8s job vs. Redwood load runner) and (3) identify any questions about model variants or quantization we should flag?

Alex — once we run the baseline qualification I’ll share a short deck with results and recommended config.

Best,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Alex / Marissa — thanks for the traces and write-up. I dug into the CSV and traces overnight; highlights and an initial test plan below.

Quick findings from sample traces:
- Majority of requests are short-turn: 1-3 prompt tokens in, 8-24 tokens out; that favors low-latency, small-batch execution rather than large batching strategies.
- Under burst windows, queueing in the current endpoint increases per-request batching which spikes p95. We can avoid that with lower-latency kernels + per-request prioritization.
- Tokenization variance appears to add ~30-80ms per request depending on language mix — we should normalize on one tokenizer and surface tokenization time in metrics.

Initial qualification/test harness proposal:
- Run a 3-stage replay: (1) baseline 150 concurrent sessions for 30m, (2) ramp to 350 for 20m, (3) peak 600 for 15m with realistic inter-arrival distribution from your CSV. Capture p50/p95/p99, streaming inter-token latencies, and tail after final token.
- Use Redwood load-runner (containerized) that replays traces token-accurately and supports streaming via chunked HTTP. We’ll provide a results dashboard and raw logs.
- Test two configs: (A) Redwood Dedicated (4x A100 equivalent reserved pool) tuned for low-latency kernels; (B) Hybrid with autoscaling + fallback to smaller quantized model for overload scenarios.

Open questions for Finly:
- Which model family are you validating against (open Llama-2/Redwood-verified variant)? Any constraints on quantization or model family for production?
- Any security/compliance blockers that would prevent us from running enclave-like measurement runs or sending traces to Redwood-managed test infra?

I’ll draft a short runbook and proposed measurable SLOs and share before the deep-dive. If Tue 10:00 PDT works for everyone, I’ll send a calendar invite with the agenda (trace review, test matrix, security checklist, logistics).

Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
